lines.text: In this lesson, you will learn to use forever loops with if-then conditions to keep checking the world, and build bouncing and wrap-around motion.
Games, animations and apps run in a loop that keeps checking what’s happening.
If-then means selection: the computer only runs the inside blocks when the condition is true.
In many classic games, things that leave one side of the screen come back on the other.
That’s a forever loop with a condition.
Every game runs a game loop: read input, update positions, check collisions, draw.
Forever + if is the heart of it.
In Python, “while True” is a forever loop, and “if” works just like the Scratch block.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
